div.head: IV Eg 1.5a
div.ab: Gif he swa earm bið, þæt he aðer deð oððe þa Godes wanað, his saula to forwyrde, oððe waccor mid modes graman hy behwyrfð þonne þæt he him to agenum teleð, ðonne him micele agenre is, þæt him æfre on écnysse gelæst, gif he hit mid unnan ⁊ mid fulre blisse dón wolde.

Gyf he swa earm bið, þæt he aþer deð oððe þa Godes wanað, his sawla to forwyrde, oððe waccor mid modes graman hy behwyrfð þonne þæt he him to agenum teleð, ðonne him micele agenre is, þæt him æfre on écnysse gelæst, gyf he hit mid unnan ⁊ fulre blisse dón wolde.

Gyf he swa earm bið þæt he aþer deð oððe þa Godes wanað, his sawla to forwyrde, oððe waccor mid modes graman hy behwyrfð þonne þæt he him to agenum teleð, þonne him micele agenre is þæt him æfre on écnysse gelæst, gyf he hit mid unnan ⁊ mid fulre blisse dón wolde.

Wenn der [Zehntpflichtige] so erbärmlich ist, dass er eine beider [folgender Handlungen] thut: entweder die Kirchen[-Gerechtsame] mindert, seiner Seele zum Verderben, oder mit Herzens Unwillen sie lässiger behandelt als was er sich zum Eigenthume zählt: bei weitem mehr ist doch sein eigen, was ihm immer in Ewigkeit bleibt, wenn er es mit Bereitwilligkeit und mit voller Freudigkeit thun wollte.

If the [tithe-payer] is so wretched that he does one of two [things]: either diminishes God's [dues], to the ruin of his soul, or with grudging heart treats them more slackly than what he counts as his own property: yet far more his own is what remains his for ever in eternity, if he would do it willingly and with full gladness.

And if he is so debased as either to curtail what is due to God, to the ruin of his soul or, with angry heart, to attend to it less diligently than to what he accounts his own, [he ought to realise that] what endures for him to all eternity will be much more his own, if he has been willing to give his tribute with gladness and with all willingness.

If he is so contemptible, that he either curtails God’s [dues] to the perdition of his soul, or with reluctance at heart attends to them less diligently than to what he accounts his own; then much more his own is what endures for him for ever into eternity if he would pay it with willingness and full gladness.
div.note: Not in the Latin Versio. In F, ‘gerihta’ or similar should be supplied after ‘þa Godes’.
Robertson supplies “he ought to realise that”, to make the sequence of thought clearer.
